$comment: documents.batchUpdate -> POST v1/documents/{documentId}:batchUpdate, request BatchUpdateDocumentRequest, response BatchUpdateDocumentResponse. Read from Google's own discovery document 2026-10-01. Google's batchUpdate takes an ARRAY of typed Request objects -- dozens of kinds (insertText, deleteContentRange, replaceAllText, updateTextStyle, insertTable, ...) -- and this action builds exactly ONE: a single insertText request. The general escape hatch (an author-supplied requests array) is deliberately NOT offered -- it needs a config shape (arbitrary polymorphic objects) nothing in this estate has used before, the same bar document_create's own deferred content field never cleared. insertText is the one operation that actually answers Fancy's complaint: a blank document created with no way to put text in it.
title: Insert text into a Google Doc
description: Insert plain text at a position in an existing document's body.
$idempotencyComment: batchUpdate declares no idempotency key. A retry inserts the text a SECOND time at the same index -- never detects or merges with the first attempt.

config.label: Document ID
config.description: From document_create's data.documentId, or the id in the document's own URL.

config.label: Text
config.description: Inserted verbatim. A newline in it starts a new paragraph, carrying the style of whatever paragraph the insertion point sits in.

config.label: Insert at index
config.description: A zero-based position in UTF-16 code units, but 0 itself is never valid -- Google's body content starts at index 1. 1 is the very beginning of a freshly created blank document. To append after existing content, read the document's own length first (not yet offered by this connector) and insert there instead.

outputShape.description: One entry per request sent -- one here. insertText's own reply carries nothing; the array is present and empty-shaped rather than a usable result.
Which estate this ran against. Google has no sandbox, so: fake or live.
